To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
soybean meal, when available, is the most economical protein source for broiler production, but peanut meal can be more economical under some conditions.
the profitability of using alternative protein supplements in broiler feed can be analyzed through the development of mathematical programming models.

the use of peanut meal in place of soybean meal is more profitable when the protein content of the diet is higher, when the price of soybean meal increases, when the price for broilers processed into carcass decreases, or when the price for the byproduct of broiler processing (livers) increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a two-stage linear mathematical program to analyze the production and profitability responses to alternative protein sources and levels in broiler rations.
the development of a mathematical program that optimally allocates resources to the production and processing of broilers.
the development of a mathematical programming model that optimizes broilers' production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soybean meal, as a protein source for broilers, is more profitable than peanut protein meal.
peanut meal is not a suitable replacement for soybean meal as a protein supplement in broiler diets.
the use of peanut meal as a substitute for soybean meal in broiler feed would not be profitable under present conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of peanut meal in poultry diets should be based on a thorough analysis of the economic and nutritional characteristics of the peanut meal, the soybean meal, and the broiler product being produced.
soybean meal should be used in broiler rations whenever feasible.
soybean meal should be the protein source of choice in broiler rations, but peanut meal can be used in some cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the profitability of alternative protein sources in feed is not simply a function of the price difference between them.
the value of marginal products concept can be used to analyze the profitability of alternative feedstuffs in a two-stage mathematical programming model.
a two-stage model is a more appropriate representation of the production process than a one-stage model.
